title: PH, Papua New Guinea seek better deals in energy, tourism
summary: SHENZHEN, China -- Philippine President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and Prime Minister James Marape are eyeing enhanced cooperation in energy and tourism.

blocks.text: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China. Photo from Presidential Communications Office
SHENZHEN, China — Philippine President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and Prime Minister James Marape are eyeing enhanced cooperation in energy and tourism.
This was discussed by the two leaders in a bilateral meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.
According to the Presidential Communications Office, Marcos also brought up opportunities to encourage Philippine investments in fisheries and port infrastructure.
“These areas of cooperation aim to enhance food security, improve connectivity, and open up more opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries,” the PCO added.
The PCO said the Philippines and Papua New Guinea are exploring new avenues for economic cooperation and mutually beneficial partnerships.
Both Marcos were in China to participate in the AELM, which was also attended by other leaders from the 21 member-economies of APEC. — BAP, GMA News
